problem: Long-horizon robot manipulation with deformable objects fails due to inconsistent demonstration quality and frame-index-based labeling brittleness.
approach: A stage-aware reward model predicts task stage and progress using natural-language subtask annotations, then filters demonstrations via Reward-Aligned Behavior Cloning.
contribution: Achieves 83% success on T-shirt folding from flattened state and 67% from crumpled, compared to 8% and 0% with vanilla BC.

problem: Natural language vehicle control must handle ambiguous commands and evolving dialogue context while maintaining protocol compliance.
approach: Unified framework combining agent-orchestrated data augmentation pipeline, reference models, and evaluation protocol to generate and assess diverse ambiguity-rich dialogues.
contribution: Achieves 15% higher parsing accuracy, 20% stronger ambiguity resolution, and 98% protocol compliance on realistic in-cabin scenarios.

problem: LLM steering requires either suboptimal signals from labeled examples or hundreds of examples with task-specific optimization procedures.
approach: COLD-Steer approximates gradient descent effects at inference time using unit kernel approximation or finite-difference methods without parameter updates.
contribution: Achieves up to 95% steering effectiveness using 50 times fewer samples than baselines.

problem: Imperfect-information games like Fog of War chess require reasoning about information gathering and opponent knowledge beyond standard search.
approach: Obscuro advances search in imperfect-information games through improved algorithms for scalable reasoning without common knowledge.
contribution: First superhuman AI for FoW chess, significantly stronger than prior state-of-the-art and human players including world's best.

problem: Multimodal LLMs hallucinate emotions, generating irrelevant content despite lacking innate emotional instincts.
approach: EmotionHallucer benchmark evaluates emotion hallucinations via adversarial QA framework grounded in emotion psychology and real-world perception.
contribution: Finds most current models exhibit substantial emotion hallucinations, with closed-source outperforming open-source and reasoning improving performance.

problem: High-resolution visual representation learning fails due to quadratic complexity of Vision Transformers and fixed scanning patterns in Mamba-based models.
approach: InfoScan learns adaptive scanning policy via reinforcement learning, assessing informativeness through entropy and local structural analysis.
contribution: Achieves superior efficiency-accuracy trade-offs across diverse tasks via information-driven dynamic scanning.

problem: Token-wise layer skipping in LLMs suffers from instability in early-exit and router-based methods requiring extensive retraining.
approach: GateSkip uses residual-stream sigmoid-linear gates on each Attention/MLP branch, enabling per-layer token skipping via gate-based ranking.
contribution: Saves up to 15% compute while retaining >90% accuracy on long-form reasoning, with stable fine-tuning on pretrained models.

problem: Training VAEs from scratch emphasizes low-level details over semantic structure for diffusion model tokenizers.
approach: AlignTok aligns pretrained visual encoders via three-stage strategy: frozen adapter-decoder, joint optimization with semantic loss, decoder refinement.
contribution: Reaches gFID of 1.90 on ImageNet 256x256 in 64 epochs, outperforming FLUX VAE and VA-VAE on text-to-image models.

problem: Molecular representations fail to capture stereochemistry and complex features at fragment level due to atom-level graphs and fixed fragment libraries.
approach: h-MINT uses OverlapBPE tokenization allowing overlapping fragments plus hierarchical model jointly capturing drug-target interactions at atom and fragment levels.
contribution: Improves binding affinity prediction by 2-4% Pearson/Spearman correlation, enhances virtual screening by 1-3% on multiple benchmarks.

problem: Reasoning language models self-jailbreak by introducing benign assumptions to justify harmful requests despite safety training.
approach: Mechanistic analysis reveals RLMs use compliance from benign reasoning training to circumvent safety guardrails by reframing harmful requests.
contribution: Shows minimal safety reasoning data during training ensures RLMs remain safety-aligned despite self-jailbreaking tendency.

problem: fMRI decoding and concept grounding struggle to capture interacting concepts and hierarchical structure from neural activity.
approach: NEURONA neuro-symbolic framework learns to decode interacting concepts via hierarchical predicate-argument dependencies grounded in fMRI.
contribution: Incorporating structure improves both decoding accuracy and generalization across brain regions.

problem: State-of-the-art policy gradient methods for text-to-image model alignment suffer from training instability and high variance due to disproportionate credit assignment.
approach: PCPO enforces proportional credit assignment through stable objective reformulation and principled timestep reweighting to mitigate model collapse.
contribution: Substantially outperforms DanceGRPO with faster convergence and superior image quality through mitigating recursive training failures.

problem: Existing time-series explanation methods fail to capture temporal context, producing fragmented point-wise explanations lacking interpretable segment boundaries.
approach: TimeSeg uses information-theoretic framework with reinforcement learning to identify contiguous subsequences maximizing mutual information with predictions.
contribution: Produces more coherent and human-understandable segment-wise explanations capturing holistic temporal patterns.

problem: Self-attention mechanisms cannot perform polyadic tasks requiring detecting correlated token triples or compositional references.
approach: Poly-attention defines generalizations of self-attention enabling arbitrary higher-order tensor computations with systematic complexity analysis.
contribution: Provides tight complexity bounds and representational strength analysis, revealing trade-offs between expressiveness and approximation time.

problem: Fine-tuning-based concept erasure is time-consuming for multiple concepts, while real-time editing degrades non-target generation quality.
approach: SPEED edits model parameters by searching null space where updates don't affect non-targets, using influence filtering, prior augmentation, and invariant constraints.
contribution: Erases 100 concepts in 5 seconds with consistent non-target preservation outperforming existing methods.

problem: Individual vision foundation models excel in specific domains but lack generality across diverse robot tasks.
approach: VER distills multiple VFMs into expert library, fine-tuning lightweight routing network for dynamic task-relevant expert selection via patchwise routing.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on 17 diverse robotic tasks with fewer than 0.4% parameters requiring fine-tuning.

problem: Local navigation policies fail to generalize across robot morphologies due to embodiment-specific dynamics and multi-modal decision problems.
approach: CE-Nav decouples universal geometric reasoning via embodiment-agnostic VelFlow from dynamics adaptation via lightweight refiner using online RL.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on quadrupeds, bipeds, quadrotors with minimal adaptation cost and successful real-world deployment.

problem: Chunked critics for multi-step value propagation require open-loop policy execution over full action chunks, causing sub-optimality in reactive environments.
approach: Decoupled Q-Chunking separates critic and policy chunk lengths via optimistic distillation of partial chunks from original chunked critic.
contribution: Retains multi-step value benefits while avoiding open-loop sub-optimality on long-horizon offline goal-conditioned benchmarks.

problem: Image-to-point cloud registration faces projection ambiguity and scale inconsistency between 2D and 3D representations.
approach: RayI2P predicts patch-wise 3D ray bundles connecting image patches to scene, then estimates pose via differentiable ray-guided regression.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art registration accuracy on KITTI and nuScenes, outperforming existing methods.

problem: Uncertainty quantification via ensembles is computationally expensive, while single-model approximations struggle.
approach: Contextual similarity distillation estimates ensemble variance with single model by reinterpreting ensemble variance as supervised regression with kernel targets.
contribution: Achieves competitive or superior performance to ensemble baselines on out-of-distribution detection and sparse-reward RL.

problem: Scaling visual geometry transformers for long image sequences faces computational and memory bottlenecks due to token collapse in global attention.
approach: FastVGGT uses training-free three-part token partitioning preserving initial frames, salient tokens, and region-based random sampling.
contribution: Achieves 4x speedup on 1000-image sequences while mitigating error accumulation without retraining.

problem: Textured 3D morphing struggles to preserve both structural coherence and appearance when extending 2D interpolation to 3D.
approach: Interp3D uses generative priors with progressive alignment, enforcing structure via SLAT-guided interpolation and fine-grained texture fusion.
contribution: Demonstrates significant advantages over previous methods in fidelity, transition smoothness, and plausibility via quantitative metrics and human studies.

problem: Full LLM fine-tuning is computationally expensive while PEFT struggles to learn new knowledge with suboptimal performance.
approach: Hybrid fine-tuning jointly updates LLMs and PEFT modules via zeroth-order and first-order methods under novel hybrid smoothness condition framework.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent performance improvement across downstream tasks and model architectures making hybrid approach viable for large-scale fine-tuning.

problem: Existing metrics for evaluating formal statement translation fail to balance semantic and structural information grounded in proof correctness.
approach: ASSESS captures syntactic structure via operator trees and computes TransTED Similarity metric incorporating semantic transformations.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and Kappa score on EPLA benchmark of 1,247 expert-annotated formal statement pairs.

problem: Discrete Flow Models require pretrained teachers or expensive finetuning for few-step acceleration without strong acceleration guarantees.
approach: PairFlow trains DFMs from coupled source-target distributions using closed-form inversion without requiring pretrained teachers.
contribution: Matches or surpasses two-stage finetuning performance with only 1.7% training compute overhead.

problem: Probabilistic forecasting of irregular time series lacks marginalization consistency between joint and marginal distributions.
approach: MOSES parametrizes stochastic process via mixture of normalizing flows with separable univariate transformations enabling analytical marginalization.
contribution: Achieves accurate joint and marginal predictions significantly outperforming ProFITi and other baselines on marginalization consistency.

problem: Model merging trades off accuracy against storage cost, with single merged models suffering large gaps from individual fine-tuned models.
approach: FlexMerge generates merged models of varying sizes spanning spectrum from single model to all individuals, supporting multiple merging algorithms.
contribution: Reveals steep accuracy gains with modest size increases (up to 13.5% when doubling) and algorithm rankings vary across size spectrum.

problem: Transformer principles from text transfer imperfectly to time series due to structural differences in data representations.
approach: Analyzes Transformers through rank structure and flow-of-ranks mechanism explaining compressibility and depth-dependent rank inflation.
contribution: Compresses Chronos foundation model achieving 65% inference time and 81% memory reduction without accuracy loss.

problem: Existing RLVR methods improve effectiveness but neglect diversity by imitating entire expert trajectories.
approach: MENTOR provides expert guidance only at critical decision points via mixed-policy framework enabling effective and diverse exploration.
contribution: Enables models to capture expert essence rather than surface imitation, achieving superior overall performance in reasoning tasks.

problem: Current information-seeking agents rely heavily on search-engine-indexed knowledge, missing unindexed sources like dynamic pages and embedded files.
approach: UIS-Digger uses multi-agent framework with dual-mode browsing enabling simultaneous webpage searching and file parsing.
contribution: Achieves 26.36% on UIS-QA benchmark with 30B backbone, outperforming systems integrating O3 and GPT-4.1 at revealing UIS limitations.

problem: Traditional Image Quality Assessment methods predict human preferences but cannot assess image usability for embodied AI tasks.
approach: Constructs perception-cognition-decision-execution pipeline with Embodied-IQA database containing 30k image pairs and 5m annotations via VLMs and real robots.
contribution: Establishes first IQA benchmark for embodied AI, demonstrating need for quality indicators tailored to robot perception under distortions.

problem: Adversarial attacks on SNNs typically modify intensities or event counts, overlooking timing-only attacks preserving spike counts and amplitudes.
approach: Spike-retiming uses projected-in-the-loop optimization with soft logits for differentiable retiming and discrete projection satisfying capacity constraints.
contribution: Achieves over 90% attack success on DVS-Gesture while touching fewer than 2% of spikes.

problem: Adapting 3D generative models for specific design tasks requires costly retraining and cannot handle seed ligands or fragments.
approach: Introduces Interpolate-Integrate and Replacement Guidance, training-free inference-time conditioning strategies for E(3)-equivariant flow-matching models.
contribution: Generates bioisosteric 3D molecules preserving shape and pharmacophore patterns for ligand hopping and fragment merging tasks.

problem: Transfer learning suffers from negative transfer where source representations harm target performance under distribution shift.
approach: Augments frozen source features with trainable target-side encoder capturing residual signals, providing theoretical guarantees against negative transfer.
contribution: Proves convergence rate no worse than training from scratch under informative distributions up to logarithmic factors.

problem: High-quality numeric labels for regression are scarce while rankings are easier to obtain from experts or AI judges.
approach: BAYES-ECR performs Bayesian update combining Gaussian regressor likelihood with Bradley-Terry ranker likelihood plus calibration for scale mismatch.
contribution: Shows 97.65% median improvement across 12 datasets over prior state-of-the-art with calibrated ranking.

problem: Protein generation benchmarks focus on functional motifs, leaving general geometric preservation capabilities untested.
approach: GeomMotif benchmark evaluates arbitrary structural fragment preservation via 57 tasks sampling from PDB with comprehensive structural characterization.
contribution: Reveals sequence-based and structure-based models find different tasks challenging, with geometric preservation varying significantly by structural context.

problem: Group-based policy gradient methods like GRPO suffer from degenerate groups erasing learning signals and synchronization barriers limiting scalability.
approach: SPO replaces per-group baselines with persistent KL-adaptive value tracker and normalizes advantages globally, enabling prioritized sampling curriculum.
contribution: Improves Qwen3-8B average maj@32 by +3.4pp over GRPO across five hard math benchmarks with +7.3pp on BRUMO 25.

problem: Existing spatio-temporal models fail to generalize to unseen regions or graph topologies, while physics-driven approaches scale poorly to complex structures.
approach: PhySTA integrates operator-based spectrum-temporal learning with Graph-Time Fourier Neural Operator plus adaptive multi-scale interaction.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while reducing computation cost and parameter overhead on large-scale benchmarks.

problem: 4-bit quantization assumed memory-optimal universally, but reasoning models show KV cache dominance requiring scale-dependent trade-offs.
approach: Systematic experiments on mathematical, code generation, and knowledge-intensive reasoning tasks establish scale-dependent quantization thresholds.
contribution: Finds models below 8-bit effective 4B parameters benefit from larger weights, while larger models prioritize test-time compute.

problem: Inference-time control in diffusion models lacks principled methods for adapting outputs to diverse test-time objectives.
approach: Framework orchestrates local and global search via breadth-first/depth-first tree search and annealed Langevin MCMC.
contribution: Demonstrates significant gains in performance and efficiency over baselines across planning, offline RL, and image generation.
